questions.stem: A 38-year-old man with untreated HIV infection is evaluated in clinic. Which of the following findings would be most indicative of a CD4+ T-cell count below 200 cells/mm³?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Squamous cell carcinoma at sites of sexual contact

explanation.summary: Candida esophagitis appears at CD4+ counts below 200, whereas oral thrush and the other listed findings appear at counts below 500.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick's table of HIV-associated infections places Candida albicans esophagitis in the CD4+ count below 200/mm³ tier, together with Cryptococcus meningitis, Cryptosporidium diarrhea, Mycobacterium avium complex, Toxoplasma brain abscesses, Histoplasma pneumonia, disseminated HHV-8, JC virus PML, and Pneumocystis pneumonia. As CD4+ counts fall, opportunistic and rare infections become more likely, and Candida progresses from oral thrush to esophagitis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Localized cutaneous Kaposi's sarcoma from HHV-8 is listed at a CD4+ count below 500; disseminated HHV-8 disease is the below-200 presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oral hairy leukoplakia from EBV is listed at a CD4+ count below 500.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oral thrush from Candida albicans is listed in the CD4+ count below 500 tier, a less advanced stage than esophagitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HPV-related squamous cell carcinoma at sites of sexual contact is listed at a CD4+ count below 500.

questions.topicName: Diagnosis and Treatment of Immunodeficiency Disorders

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man with active pulmonary Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection develops a secondary immunodeficiency. Which of the following best describes the mechanism by which this infection impairs immune function?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apoptosis and necrosis of antigen-presenting cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased neutrophil chemotaxis and phagocytic killing

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct depletion of circulating CD4+ T cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disruption of the epithelial barrier surface

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loss of circulating memory B cells

explanation.summary: Tuberculosis causes secondary immunodeficiency through increased apoptosis and necrosis of antigen-presenting cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the infectious causes of secondary immunodeficiency, the brick states that Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection leads to increased apoptosis and necrosis of antigen-presenting cells. Each of the distractors is a mechanism the brick attributes to a different cause of secondary immunodeficiency.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Decreased chemotaxis and phagocytosis describe the effects of glucocorticoids and of aging, not TB.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Direct targeting of CD4+ T cells with resulting lymphopenia is the mechanism of HIV infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Disruption of the epithelial barrier is the mechanism of major trauma or burn.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Loss of memory B cells is the mechanism of measles-associated immunosuppression.

questions.topicName: Diagnosis and Treatment of Immunodeficiency Disorders

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis is started on a TNF-α inhibitor. Which of the following immune processes is most directly impaired by this medication?

explanation.summary: TNF-α inhibitors downregulate cytokine expression and can impair granuloma formation.
explanation.whyCorrect: In its list of immunosuppressive medications that cause secondary immunodeficiency, the brick states that TNF-α inhibitors downregulate cytokine expression, which can affect granuloma formation. This is the specific immune process the brick ties to this class of cytokine inhibitor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Loss of B cells is the effect of rituximab (anti-CD20), a monoclonal antibody with a different target.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Complement activation is not the process the brick links to TNF-α inhibitors; complement defects are inborn errors of immunity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mucosal barrier disruption is the mechanism of cystic fibrosis, not of cytokine inhibition.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neutrophil oxidative burst is defective in chronic granulomatous disease, not as an effect of TNF-α inhibition.

questions.topicName: Diagnosis and Treatment of Immunodeficiency Disorders

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman receives rituximab for lymphoma. Several months later she develops recurrent sinopulmonary infections. Which of the following changes is most directly responsible for her increased susceptibility to infection?

explanation.summary: Rituximab, an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, induces loss of B cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick explains that the effects of monoclonal antibodies depend on their target, and gives rituximab (anti-CD20) as the example that induces loss of B cells. B-cell depletion removes the source of antibody production, predisposing to the recurrent sinopulmonary infections seen with humoral defects.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Late complement deficiencies are inborn errors of immunity that predispose to Neisseria infection; they are not drug induced.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Impaired chemotaxis is an effect of glucocorticoids and aging, not of rituximab.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Loss of CD4+ T cells is the mechanism of HIV infection, not of anti-CD20 therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Loss of splenic function occurs with sickle cell disease or splenectomy, not with rituximab.

questions.topicName: Diagnosis and Treatment of Immunodeficiency Disorders

questions.stem: An 84-year-old woman has had two episodes of community-acquired pneumonia in the past year. She takes no immunosuppressive medications and has no chronic illness. Her HIV screen, hemoglobin A1c, and serum immunoglobulin levels are all normal. Which of the following best explains her increased risk of infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone marrow invasion by an occult hematologic neoplasm

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased chemotaxis, phagocytosis, and cytokine production

choices.label: C
choices.text: Disruption of the normal mucosal barrier of the airway

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loss of memory B cells after a recent viral infection

explanation.summary: Older adults have increased infection risk because of decreased chemotaxis, phagocytosis, and cytokine production.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists extremes of age among the other causes of secondary immunodeficiency, stating that older adults have an increased risk of infection due to decreased chemotaxis, phagocytosis, and cytokine production. With medications, HIV, diabetes, and hypogammaglobulinemia excluded, her advanced age is the most likely explanation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nothing in the stem suggests a hematologic neoplasm, and marrow invasion would be expected to produce abnormal blood counts or immunoglobulins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mucosal barrier disruption is the mechanism in cystic fibrosis, which she does not have.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Her immunoglobulin levels are normal, so loss of immunoglobulins through the gut or kidney is not the explanation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Loss of memory B cells is the mechanism of post-measles immunosuppression, and no recent viral infection is described.

questions.topicName: Diagnosis and Treatment of Immunodeficiency Disorders

questions.stem: A neonate born at 26 weeks' gestation develops bacterial sepsis in the neonatal intensive care unit. Which of the following best explains this infant's increased susceptibility to infection?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Defective signaling through the IL-2 receptor γ chain

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immature innate and adaptive immune systems

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loss of circulating memory B cells

explanation.summary: Extremely premature infants have an immature innate and adaptive immune system, a secondary cause of immunodeficiency.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists extremes in age as a cause of secondary immunodeficiency and states that neonates, especially extremely premature infants, have an immature innate and adaptive immune system. The pediatric evaluation schema likewise directs clinicians to rule out prematurity before attributing infections to an inborn error of immunity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Absence of thymic tissue describes DiGeorge syndrome, an IEI with syndromic features, not the expected state of a premature infant.
whyWrongByChoice.B: IL-2Rγ chain deficiency causes X-linked SCID, a rare IEI; prematurity itself is the far more likely explanation here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A defective oxidative burst causes chronic granulomatous disease with catalase-positive abscesses, not generalized neonatal susceptibility.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Loss of memory B cells is the mechanism of post-measles immunosuppression.

questions.stem: A public health program in a region where malaria is endemic aims to reduce rates of severe malaria among undernourished children. Supplementation with which of the following has been shown to significantly lower rates of severe malaria?

explanation.summary: Zinc or vitamin A supplementation can significantly lower rates of severe malaria in endemic countries.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick's clinical correlation on undernourishment notes that adequate intake of vitamins such as C, D, and E and minerals such as zinc and selenium is essential for immune function, and gives the specific example that zinc or vitamin A supplementation can significantly lower rates of severe malaria in endemic countries. Zinc is the only option to which the brick attributes this effect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Selenium is named as an essential mineral for immune function, but the malaria example is specific to zinc and vitamin A.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Vitamin C is listed as essential for maintaining immune function, but the brick does not attribute reduced severe malaria to it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vitamin D is listed as an essential nutrient for immune function, not as the supplement shown to reduce severe malaria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vitamin E is listed as essential for immune function, without a stated effect on malaria severity.

questions.topicName: Diagnosis and Treatment of Immunodeficiency Disorders

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man sustains burns over 40% of his body surface area and subsequently develops recurrent wound infections and bacteremia. Which of the following best explains his increased susceptibility to infection?

explanation.summary: Major trauma or burn causes secondary immunodeficiency by disrupting the epithelial barrier.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists major trauma or burn among the other causes of secondary immunodeficiency, explaining that it disrupts the epithelial barrier. The adult history should also include recent trauma disrupting the skin barrier as a predisposing factor for infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone marrow suppression is an effect of cancer chemotherapeutics and marrow-invading neoplasms, not of burns.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hyperglycemia affecting neutrophil function and cytokine production is the mechanism in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Loss of immunoglobulins is the mechanism of chronic kidney disease and protein-losing enteropathy, not burns.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Loss of memory B cells is the mechanism of post-measles immunosuppression.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman has had four confirmed bacterial sinus infections in the past year. She takes no medications, has no chronic medical conditions or recent trauma, and denies HIV risk factors, and no anatomic cause for her infections is identified. A CBC with differential is normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Empiric immunoglobulin replacement therapy without testing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Genetic testing for an inborn error of immunity right away

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immunoglobulin levels, vaccine titers, and lymphocyte subsets

choices.label: D
choices.text: No further immunodeficiency evaluation at this time

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oxidative burst assay and review of the peripheral blood smear

explanation.summary: When no secondary cause is found in an adult with warning-sign infections, proceed to immunoglobulin levels, post-vaccination antibody titers, and B- and T-cell subsets.
explanation.whyCorrect: The adult evaluation schema first asks whether any medical condition, infection, medication, or anatomic cause explains the infections. When the answer is no, the brick directs an immunodeficiency evaluation consisting of a CBC with differential, immunoglobulin levels (IgA, IgG, and IgM), post-vaccination antibody titer, and B- and T-cell subsets. She meets the recurrent-infection threshold, so this workup is indicated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Immunoglobulin replacement is a treatment for a documented antibody deficiency; her immunoglobulin levels have not yet been measured.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Genetic testing is reserved for when a specific IEI is suspected after the initial laboratory evaluation, not as the next step.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immunodeficiency evaluation is not needed only when a secondary cause is identified; here none is, so evaluation should proceed.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The oxidative burst assay and smear evaluate phagocytic defects, which present with catalase-positive abscesses rather than recurrent sinusitis.

questions.stem: A 4-month-old boy with recurrent infections is noted on examination to have a cleft palate and a heart murmur. These findings most suggest an inborn error of immunity involving a defect in which of the following?

explanation.summary: Cleft palate and a heart murmur are syndromic features of DiGeorge syndrome, a cell-mediated IEI caused by a thymic defect.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick's pediatric physical examination directs clinicians to look for syndromic features, giving cleft palate and a heart murmur as findings that may indicate DiGeorge syndrome. DiGeorge syndrome is classified among the cell-mediated immunodeficiencies as a defect in the thymus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ADA deficiency causes ADA-SCID through a defect in an enzyme critical to lymphocyte development, without these syndromic features.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cytoskeletal defects cause Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome, not the craniofacial and cardiac findings of DiGeorge syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IL-2Rγ chain deficiency causes X-linked SCID, which is not associated with cleft palate or cardiac defects.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A defective oxidative burst causes chronic granulomatous disease, a phagocytic defect without syndromic features.

questions.topicName: Diagnosis and Treatment of Immunodeficiency Disorders

questions.stem: A 3-year-old boy is diagnosed with chronic granulomatous disease after an abnormal neutrophil oxidative burst assay. Which of the following is the most appropriate long-term management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antimicrobial treatment of an underlying infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prophylactic antibiotics and antifungals plus IFN-γ

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vaccination with all available live vaccines

explanation.summary: Phagocytic defects such as CGD are managed with prophylactic antibiotics and antifungals in addition to IFN-γ.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that management of an IEI depends on the defect, and that phagocytic defects like chronic granulomatous disease require prophylactic antibiotics and antifungals in addition to IFN-γ. Both bacteria and fungi cause the catalase-positive abscesses of CGD, hence the combined prophylaxis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antimicrobials to remove an infectious cause treat secondary immunodeficiency caused by infection, not the lifelong killing defect of CGD.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Discontinuing or modifying an immunosuppressant treats a drug-induced secondary immunodeficiency; CGD is an inborn error of immunity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immunoglobulin replacement with or without prophylactic antimicrobials is the management of antibody deficiency, not of a phagocytic defect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Live vaccines are contraindicated in severely immunocompromised patients; the brick advises vaccinating with all but live vaccines when not contraindicated.

questions.topicName: Diagnosis and Treatment of Immunodeficiency Disorders

questions.stem: A 4-month-old boy is diagnosed with X-linked SCID due to IL-2 receptor γ chain deficiency. He is started on immunoglobulin replacement and prophylactic antimicrobials. Which of the following is the most appropriate definitive treatment?

explanation.summary: T-cell defects and combined immunodeficiencies such as X-linked SCID may require hematopoietic stem cell transplant.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that T cell defects or combined immunodeficiencies may require hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT), and its review question explanation lists X-SCID first among the severe or combined immunodeficiencies for which HSCT should be performed. Immunoglobulin replacement and prophylactic antimicrobials reduce infections but do not correct the underlying T-cell defect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Genetic testing is a diagnostic step; it does not treat the infant's immunodeficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IFN-γ is part of the management of phagocytic defects such as CGD, not of SCID.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immunoglobulin replacement treats antibody deficiency; it does not restore the absent T-cell function in X-SCID.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prophylactic antimicrobials decrease infection frequency but are supportive, not definitive, for a combined immunodeficiency.
